t: A Berber dynasty of Almohad origin that ruled Ifriqiya, roughly modern Tunisia and eastern Algeria, from Tunis between 1229 and 1574.
Tunis prospered on grain, wool and leather exports and on treaties that let Italian and Catalan merchants trade under their own consuls.
Squeezed between Habsburg Spain and the Ottomans in the sixteenth century, the dynasty fell when Ottoman forces took Tunis in 1574.
dyk: In 1257 an embassy from the king of Kanem, near Lake Chad, crossed the Sahara and presented the Hafsid ruler al-Mustansir with a giraffe, which caused a sensation in Tunis.
ev: Abu Zakariya Yahya breaks with the Almohad caliph and rules Ifriqiya independently from Tunis
Al-Mustansir takes the caliphal title of commander of the faithful
Louis IX of France dies near Tunis during the Eighth Crusade
Ibn Khaldun is born in Tunis
The Marinid sultan Abu al-Hasan briefly occupies Tunis
Reign of Abu Faris Abd al-Aziz II restores Hafsid power
Charles V takes Tunis and makes the Hafsid sultan a Spanish vassal
Sinan Pasha’s Ottoman forces take Tunis and end the dynasty
